info: Matter commonly exists as solids, liquids, and gases. Solids have a definite shape and volume because their particles are closely packed and vibrate in fixed positions. Liquids have a definite volume but no fixed shape because their particles can move past one another. Gases have no fixed shape or volume because their particles are far apart and move freely in all directions.

questions.questionText: Which state of matter has a definite shape and a definite volume?

options: Very close and fixed in place

questions.questionText: Which statement best describes particle movement in a solid?
options: Particles move freely in all directions
